agree.reason: Opening with her own $600,000 figure and saying the product sits on top of the warehouse system gives Dana a reason to read and a short answer for her IT director, but nothing turns the result into dollars she would save, so a call is plausible but not compelling.

honest.reason: The body's 4.1-to-1.9 figure is accurate and credited to one customer, but the subject line says that customer's wrong-item returns fell by more than half when the data measures mis-picks, and leaving out the other customer's 2.8-to-2.2 result makes the best case look typical.

works_the_facts.reason: It quotes the raw rates but never works out what they mean for her: a cut of about 54%, roughly $300,000 a year against her $600,000, and a cost of about $75,000 a year for 5 sites at $1,250 each.

right_comparison.reason: It mentions the $600,000 status quo only as a hook and never sets it against what she would save or what the software costs, so the alternative of doing nothing is not laid out.

qualification.reason: A result from one customer needs a checkable hedge, such as the range across customers or a pilot target with a number and a date, and the email gives none.

objections.reason: It meets the IT objection directly by saying the product doesn't replace the warehouse system, needs no re-platforming and takes three weeks to set up, though it could also say how little it asks of her IT team.

fit.reason: It is short, has four tight paragraphs and a clear ask, and reads easily on a phone as the brief asked.
